title: Types & styles of mountaineering
intro: Mountaineering includes everything from non-technical mountain travel to steep, technical climbing. Terrain, exposure, altitude and remoteness shape the skills and equipment needed; a style describes how an objective is approached, not a universal grade.
heroAlt: An ice climber ascending a steep alpine ice route

sections.heading: Choosing a discipline
sections.text: A route may combine several disciplines: a trek can approach a glacier, an alpine climb can include rock and ice, and a ski tour can cross glaciated terrain. Match the objective to current team skills, conditions and equipment, and seek qualified instruction before attempting technical ground.
sections.alt: A small group hiking along a mountain trail

sections.heading: Alpine style and siege style
sections.text: In alpine style, a small team carries its supplies and climbs continuously, generally without fixing a route or establishing a chain of stocked camps. Siege style uses a larger expedition, fixed ropes and successive camps supplied by repeated carries; it can support acclimatization and logistics on very high peaks but requires more time and resources. These are broad approaches, not rigid categories, and real expeditions may mix methods.
sections.alt: Expedition tents at a high-altitude glacier base camp
facts: Alpine style emphasizes a light, continuous push by a small team.
Siege style uses camps and repeated supply carries; neither style guarantees safety.

modules.heading: Seven common types
modules.intro: Difficulty labels are relative: route grades, weather, altitude, remoteness and a climber's experience can change the real demands.

cards.title: Alpine climbing
cards.description: Climbing a mountain route that may combine rock, snow and ice, often with long approaches and changing conditions.
cards.terrain: Ridges, glaciers, mixed faces and high passes.
cards.skill: Intermediate to expert; depends strongly on route.
cards.gear: Helmet, harness, rope, protection, crampons, ice axe, navigation and weather layers.
cards.alt: A climber using ice tools on a steep alpine route

cards.title: Expedition / Himalayan climbing
cards.description: Remote, high-altitude climbing with complex logistics, extended acclimatization and camps. Expeditions may use alpine, siege or hybrid styles.
cards.terrain: Very high snow, ice, glaciers and exposed ridges.
cards.skill: Advanced; requires prior altitude and technical experience.
cards.gear: Expedition clothing, high-altitude boots, shelter, communications and objective-specific climbing kit.
cards.alt: A high-altitude expedition camp with many tents on a glacier

cards.title: Rock climbing
cards.description: Progress on rock faces using hands and feet, with protection and belaying appropriate to the route.
cards.terrain: Crags, cliffs, ridges and multi-pitch walls.
cards.skill: Beginner to expert; routes are graded by technical difficulty.
cards.gear: Climbing shoes, helmet, harness, rope, belay device and route-specific protection.
cards.alt: A climber ascending a steep rock face

cards.title: Ice climbing
cards.description: Climbing frozen water or alpine ice using specialized tools and protection.
cards.terrain: Frozen waterfalls, gullies and ice faces.
cards.skill: Intermediate to expert; ice quality and temperature vary.
cards.gear: Helmet, harness, crampons, ice tools, screws and insulating layers.
cards.alt: A climber climbing a steep ice pitch with technical ice tools

cards.title: Mixed climbing
cards.description: Climbing a route that alternates between rock, ice and snow, requiring transitions between movement techniques.
cards.terrain: Alpine gullies, frozen cliffs and rocky winter faces.
cards.skill: Advanced; requires solid rock and ice skills.
cards.gear: Helmet, harness, technical tools, crampons, rope and mixed protection.
cards.alt: A climber negotiating a mixed rock-and-ice route

cards.title: Ski mountaineering
cards.description: Travel and climb on skis, sometimes carrying skis on steep sections and skiing a planned descent.
cards.terrain: Snow-covered slopes, glaciers and high passes.
cards.skill: Advanced downhill skiing plus avalanche, navigation and glacier skills.
cards.gear: Touring skis and bindings, skins, boots, beacon, shovel, probe, helmet and glacier kit as required.
cards.alt: Steve Marolt skiing the northeast ridge of Everest

cards.title: Hiking and scrambling
cards.description: Mountain walking ranges from marked trails to hands-on scrambling over non-technical rock; some scrambling routes have serious exposure.
cards.terrain: Paths, ridges, scree and easy rock steps.
cards.skill: Beginner to advanced, depending on navigation and exposure.
cards.gear: Suitable boots, weather layers, map, compass or GPS, food, water and a headlamp.
cards.alt: A small group hiking along a mountain trail

rows.objective: Climb and ski a mountain route
